title: Review findings: acme-shop #412 and #415
subtitle: The 11 review comments on two open PRs, each next to its code. Pick what to do with each; my recommendation is starred.
tldr: Fix 6 in the PRs, ticket 2, decline 2; 1 resolves itself. Two are real bugs these PRs introduce: #412 gives no discount at exactly 10 or 50 units, and #415 can authorize a card twice when PayCo times out after accepting. Both are one-line fixes; neither PR should merge before them.
changes: `docs/pricing.md` is now a ticket, not a fix in #412: its order of operations needs a product decision from the PRICING-88 owner.

blocks.md: Two review agents read the PRs at the heads below and posted with your `gh` login, so every comment on GitHub reads as yours. I checked each finding against the code before recommending.

sections.title: #412 · bulk discount tiers
sections.lead: 3 bugs this PR introduces, 1 test gap, 3 smaller comments. Diff: `main` `89efd8e` → head `62ccc86`, limited to the commented files.

items.text: `tierFor` gives no tier at exactly 10 or 50 units
items.sub: Recommend fix in PR: The spec says "10 or more"; `>` drops both thresholds. One character.
items.detail:
**Reviewer:** `TIERS.find((t) => qty > t.minQty)` excludes the threshold, so 10 units get no discount and 50 units get 5 % instead of 10 %.

**My reasoning:** the file header (`src/pricing/tiers.ts:2`) quotes PRICING-88 as "10 or more … 50 or more". `lineTotal({qty: 10, unitCents: 100})` returns 1000, the undiscounted price. The fix is one character in a file this PR adds.

**Fix:** `TIERS.find((t) => qty >= t.minQty)` at `src/pricing/tiers.ts:17`.

**Verify:** `tierFor(10)?.percent === 5` and `tierFor(50)?.percent === 10` (the boundary tests below).

items.text: Tiered line totals are fractional cents
items.sub: Recommend fix in PR: Without a coupon the fraction reaches VAT and the payment request.
items.detail:
**Reviewer:** `gross * (1 - tier.percent / 100)` returns 3163.5 for 3 × 1110 cents at 5 %.

**My reasoning:** `applyCoupon` rounds only when a coupon is present (`src/pricing/discounts.ts:14`). Without one, the subtotal stays fractional and `addTax` rounds once more, so line and order totals can disagree by a cent. Every other money path in the repo uses integer cents (`docs/pricing.md:3`).

**Fix:** `Math.round(gross * (100 - tier.percent) / 100)`, the form `applyCoupon` already uses.

**Verify:** `Number.isInteger(lineTotal({qty: 3, unitCents: 1110}))`.

items.sub: Recommend fix in PR: A 15 % coupon would show on the receipt as a bulk saving.
items.detail:
**Reviewer:** savings are gross-with-tax minus the final total, so the coupon counts as a bulk saving.

**My reasoning:** `src/orders/createOrder.ts:16` subtracts `totalCents`, which already includes the coupon. The field name promises the tier saving, so every caller will read it that way; with a coupon it isn't.

**Fix:** `addTax(gross) - addTax(sum of lineTotal)`, before the coupon.

**Verify:** a 20-unit order with a 15 % coupon reports savings equal to 5 % of gross plus VAT.

items.text: Tier tests stop short of both thresholds
items.sub: Recommend fix in PR: The cases use 5 and 60 units, so they pass with the off-by-one.
items.detail:
**Reviewer:** the tests never touch a threshold.

**My reasoning:** the three cases (`test/tiers.test.ts:5-15`) use 5 and 60 units. Neither sits on a threshold, so all three pass with the `>` bug present.

**Fix:** four `it` cases in `test/tiers.test.ts`: 9 → none, 10 → 5 %, 49 → 5 %, 50 → 10 %.

**Verify:** the 10 and 50 cases fail on the current head and pass after the `>=` fix.

items.text: `docs/pricing.md` still says there are no bulk discounts
items.sub: Recommend ticket: The pricing spec needs a tier step; the PR is right without it.
items.detail:
**Reviewer:** `docs/pricing.md:11` still says "There are no bulk discounts".

**My reasoning:** the doc is the pricing spec for every flow, and its order of operations (lines 5-9) needs a tier step, which is a product decision for PRICING-88's owner. This PR doesn't touch the file, and the code is right without it.

**Fix:** a ticket for the PRICING-88 owner: add tiers to the order of operations (sum lines, apply tiers, apply coupon, add VAT).

**Reply I'd post:** "Agreed; ticketed (PRICING-91) so the spec change gets its own review."

items.sub: Recommend decline: It's a range lookup over 2 sorted tiers; a Map wouldn't remove the scan.
items.detail:
**Reviewer:** a `Map` would make the lookup O(1).

**My reasoning:** the lookup is a range match, not a key match: `tierFor(37)` needs the highest tier at or below 37, which a `Map` can't answer without the same scan. With 2 tiers the scan is free, and the array's order is the rule.

**Reply I'd post:** "Not taken: it's a range lookup over 2 sorted tiers, so a Map wouldn't remove the scan."

items.text: PR description says every tier is tested
items.sub: Recommend resolve after the tests: The boundary tests make the sentence true; nothing else to change.
items.detail:
**Reviewer:** the description says "tests cover every tier"; only the 10 % tier has a positive test.

**My reasoning:** with the boundary tests, every tier and both thresholds are covered, so the sentence becomes accurate.

**Reply I'd post:** "Covered by the boundary tests in <sha>."

sections.title: #415 · retry PayCo authorization
sections.lead: 1 bug this PR introduces, 1 behaviour gap, 2 smaller comments. Diff: `main` `89efd8e` → head `0a46a97`, limited to the two commented files.

items.text: A retry can authorize the card twice
items.sub: Recommend fix in PR: A timeout after PayCo accepted the call becomes a second authorization.
items.detail:
**Reviewer:** the retry re-POSTs `/v2/authorizations` with no idempotency key. If the first call succeeds but the response times out, the retry authorizes the card again.

**My reasoning:** `src/orders/charge.ts:17-21` sends only amount, currency and reference; `src/payments/paycoClient.ts` sets no default header. The 10 s client timeout makes "accepted but timed out" a realistic case. *Unverified:* that PayCo deduplicates on `Idempotency-Key`; their public docs say so, but I haven't seen it in the sandbox.

**Fix:** pass `{ headers: { "Idempotency-Key": orderId } }` as the third argument to `payco.post`.

**Verify (required):** in the PayCo sandbox, two calls with the same key return the same authorization id; the unit test asserts both attempts carry the same key.

items.sub: Recommend fix in PR: The doc comment says network errors and 5xx; the `catch` retries everything.
items.detail:
**Reviewer:** a 402 decline is retried twice more, adding 750 ms before the customer sees it.

**My reasoning:** the comment at `src/orders/charge.ts:12` promises "network errors and 5xx"; the `catch` at line 23 doesn't look at the status.

**Fix:** in the `catch`, rethrow when `err.response?.status` is below 500.

**Verify:** a test where the first call rejects with status 402 expects one call and a thrown error.

items.text: Worst case blocks checkout for 31.5 s
items.sub: Recommend ticket: Real, but the timeout budget is a checkout decision, not this PR's.
items.detail:
**Reviewer:** 3 attempts × 10 s timeout plus backoff is 31.5 s worst case, past checkout's 15 s gateway timeout.

**My reasoning:** `src/payments/paycoClient.ts:5` sets 10 s for every PayCo call, including refunds. Lowering it here changes those too. The fix needs a budget from the checkout owners: per-attempt timeout, attempts, and what the customer sees when it runs out.

**Reply I'd post:** "Agreed it's too long; ticketed (PAY-34) so checkout can set the budget."

items.sub: Recommend decline: Used once, inside the loop it controls.
items.detail:
**Reviewer:** `250 * attempt` is a magic number; make it a constant.

**My reasoning:** the number appears once, inside the retry loop it controls (`src/orders/charge.ts:25`), and nothing else reads it. A constant would move it away from the only place it means anything.

**Reply I'd post:** "Not taken: it's used once, inside the loop it controls."
